entries.test: Public communications, testimony, or reporting documenting White House pressure on Nvidia to rehire Huang would settle the claim.
entries.note: Marcus presents the earlier speculation as apparently confirmed; the proposition preserves that qualification.

entries.test: Public statements, records, or testimony establishing whether the administration offered Nvidia's board pardons or comparable assurances against prosecution would settle the claim.
entries.note: The surrounding quotation gives 'something like it' a concrete reading: assurances concerning prosecution.

entries.test: Nvidia trading data together with publicly documented investor positions or losses during the preceding two weeks would establish whether some investors suffered substantial losses.
entries.note: The absence of a precise dollar threshold does not prevent checking substantial investor losses.

entries.test: Investor lawsuit filings and resulting public disclosures would establish whether investors who lost money sued and forced substantial information about the Huang controversy into public view.
entries.note: The proposition extracts the litigation and disclosure predictions. No deadline is stated.
'Presumably' qualifies the prediction; 'probably' preserves that uncertainty.

entries.test: Published investigative reporting and documented journalistic work on the Huang story and ensuing litigation over multiple years would test the prediction.
entries.note: The embedded post is Marcus's own, explicitly reaffirmed by 'One thing I know for sure.' The multiyear horizon has not elapsed.
